summary: You can now run a standard Node.js web server on AWS Lambda with Lambda Web Functions, a new type of Lambda function reimagined for web workloads. You get a public HTTPS endpoint with no adapter layer and no servers or load balancers to manage. Node.js frameworks such as Express, Fastify, and Hono run without changes. Each execution environment handles many requests at once, and you can deploy to multiple Regions behind a single URL for lower latency. Active-CPU billing keeps the cost of waiting low, with memory and requests billed separately. Links to resources here: https://go.aws/4i4BAme. summary: You ask your AI assistant for insights and get a wall of text back but you wanted a chart, or a dashboard you can filter. MCP Apps adds a UI layer to MCP so your server can render interactive dashboards, forms, and visualizations right inside the conversation. MCP Apps is an extension to the core MCP specification (inspired by MCP-UI and the OpenAI Apps SDK) that adds a UI layer to MCP. Instead of returning a wall of text, your MCP server returns an entire HTML mini-app the host renders inside the conversation: interactive dashboards, forms, visualizations, and real-time results. summary: I built a REST API that tells dad jokes. Call it with a joke ID and it returns the joke as JSON. That one request is the whole concept. From there: what a REST API actually is, and how to build your own on AWS with API Gateway and Lambda. A REST API explained from the ground up, then built on AWS. It starts with a working dad joke API: call it with a joke ID and it returns the joke as JSON. From there, the concepts: an API as a contract, the four parts of a request (method, path, headers, optional body), the three parts of a response (status code, headers, body), what REST (Representational State Transfer) means in practice, how CRUD maps to GET/POST/PUT/DELETE, the common status codes (200, 404, 400, 500), and why REST being stateless makes Lambda a natural fit. summary: Every token in your prompt costs money, and if a prompt runs thousands of times a day, a sloppy one adds up fast. Amazon Bedrock prompt optimization rewrites your prompts for a specific model so you get better output in fewer total tokens. Amazon Bedrock has a built-in tool that rewrites your prompts for you. Prompt optimization comes in two versions. Simple optimization is one click on the magic wand: you get a side-by-side of your original prompt and an optimized one for the model you picked, in seconds. Advanced optimization runs an asynchronous job: you give it a prompt template, example inputs, ground truth, and an evaluation method, and Bedrock tests the prompt across up to five models, scores the responses, and keeps rewriting until quality improves.
